rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The anṣāb are idols erected for worship.
rows.anchor: أي الأصنام التي نصبت للعبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the azlām were explained earlier in the sūra.
rows.anchor: سبق تفسيرها في أول السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rijs means filth that sound minds find repellent; it is singular as the predicate of wine, with predicates of the coordinated nouns omitted or an omitted genitive understood as engaging in wine and gambling.
rows.anchor: قذر تعاف عنه العقول، وأفرده لأنه خبر للخمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These practices are attributed to Satan because they result from his enticement and embellishment.
rows.anchor: لأنه مسبب عن تسويله وتزيينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in the command may refer to the filth, the things just mentioned, or engaging in them.
rows.anchor: الضمير للرجس أو لما ذكر أو للتعاطي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Avoiding these things is the means by which the believers may attain success.
rows.anchor: لعلكم تفلحون } لكي تفلحوا بالاجتناب عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition is reinforced by innamā, pairing wine and gambling with idols and divining arrows, calling them filth and Satan's work, and commanding avoidance as the route to success; the next verse details their worldly and religious harms.
rows.anchor: أكد تحريم الخمر والميسر في هذه الآية، بأن صدر الجملة ب { إنما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every report means either the punishment itself or a threat of punishment; its appointed settling is the time it occurs, when its truth will be known in this world and the next.
rows.anchor: خبر يريد به إما بالعذاب أو الإيعاد به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their hostile discourse consists of denying, mocking, and attacking God's signs.
rows.anchor: بالتكذيب والاستهزاء بها والطعن فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turn away by not sitting with them and by getting up from their company.
rows.anchor: فلا تجالسهم وقم عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in 'other discourse' refers to the meaning of the signs, since the signs here are the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: أعاد الضمير على معنى الآيات لأنها القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan may distract the Prophet through whispering until he forgets the prohibition.
rows.anchor: بأن يشغلك بوسوسته حتى تنسى النهي

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads the verb with a doubled nūn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر { ينسينك } بالتشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This means after you remember the prohibition.
rows.anchor: بعد أن تذكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explicit description 'wrongdoers' replaces a pronoun to show that they wronged by substituting denial and mockery for belief and reverence.
rows.anchor: فوضع الظاهر موضع المضمر دلالة على أنهم ظلموا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who fear God do not bear responsibility for the objectionable deeds and words, or the accounting, of the people with whom they sit.
rows.anchor: وما يلزم المتقين من قبائح أعمالهم وأقوالهم الذين يجالسونهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They must remind the offenders, restrain them, and show disapproval; dhikrā may be an accusative verbal noun or nominative, 'but a reminder is incumbent.' It cannot be coordinated with the preceding negative phrase or with 'anything' because of the syntax and the positive context of min.
rows.anchor: ولكن عليهم أن يذكروهم ذكرى ويمنعوهم عن الخوض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun may refer to the offenders, who might desist from embarrassment or reluctance to distress their companions, or to the mindful, who might preserve their piety from being undermined by company.
rows.anchor: يجتنبون ذلك حياء أو كراهة لمساءتهم، ويحتمل أن يكون الضمير للذين يتقون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Muslims said that leaving whenever the Qur'an was mocked would prevent them from sitting and circumambulating in the Sacred Mosque; the verse was then revealed.
rows.anchor: أن المسلمين قالوا لئن كنا نقوم كلما استهزءوا بالقرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God splits grain and date stones to produce plants and trees; another explanation takes the phrase as the actual cleft in wheat and a date stone.
rows.anchor: بالنبات والشجر. وقيل المراد به الشقاق الذي في الحنطة والنواة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The living means growing animals and plants, matching what precedes; the dead means non-growing things such as sperm drops and seeds.
rows.anchor: يريد به ما ينمو من الحيوان والنبات ليطابق ما قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dead brought out of the living are those same non-growing things produced from animals and plants.
rows.anchor: ومخرج ذلك من الحيوان والنبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominal form 'bringing out' matches 'splitter'; the preceding verbal 'brings out the living' functions as an explanation of it.
rows.anchor: ومخرج ذلك من الحيوان والنبات، ذكره بلفظ يالاسم حملا على فالق الحب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who gives life and death is the one alone deserving worship.
rows.anchor: أي ذلكم المحيي المميت هو الذي يحق له العبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question rebukes those who turn away from God toward another.
rows.anchor: تصرفون عنه إلى غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase can mean splitting the dawn's column from night-darkness or from daylight's whiteness, or splitting the darkness of early dawn, the dimness just before morning.
rows.anchor: شاق عمود الصبح عن ظلمة الليل أو عن بياض النهار، أو شاق ظلمة الإصباح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iṣbāḥ is originally the verbal noun of aṣbaḥa, 'to enter morning,' and is used for dawn itself.
rows.anchor: والإصباح في الأصل مصدر أصبح إذا دخل في الصباح سمي به الصبح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hamza is also read with fatḥa as a plural; another reading puts al-iṣbāḥ in the accusative as a praise expression.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بفتح الهمزة على الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night is rest because the day's fatigue settles through repose, or because creatures dwell in it; the latter sense is linked to 27:86.
rows.anchor: يسكن إليه التعب بالنهار لاستراحته فيه من سكن إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative may depend on an implied verb, as jaʿil has past-tense force, supported by the Kūfan reading wa-jaʿala al-layl and by fāliq meaning falaqa; alternatively it may depend on jaʿil if the making is continuously renewed across times.
rows.anchor: ونصبه بفعل دل عليه جاعل لا به

rows.speaker: قراءة الكوفيين
rows.claim: The Kūfan readers recite the verb in the past tense, wa-jaʿala al-layl, construing it with the preceding phrase.
rows.anchor: ويدل عليه قراءة الكوفيين { وجعل اليل } حملا على معنى المعطوف عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sun and moon may coordinate with the syntactic position of al-layl, supported by their genitive reading; the author prefers taking them as accusatives governed by an implied jaʿala.
rows.anchor: ويشهد له قراءتهما بالجر والأحسن نصبهما بجعل مقدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun and moon are also read in the nominative, with an omitted predicate meaning 'made' or 'appointed.'
rows.anchor: وقرىء بالرفع على الابتداء والخبر محذوف أي مجعولان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They move in differing calculated cycles by which times are reckoned and serve as instruments of reckoning; ḥusbān is either a verbal noun of ḥasaba or a plural of ḥisāb like shihāb/shuhbān.
rows.anchor: على أدوار مختلفة يحسب بهما الأوقات ويكونان علمي الحسبان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That points to making the sun and moon instruments for reckoning time.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى جعلهما حسبانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Almighty has subdued the sun and moon and set them moving in their particular courses.
rows.anchor: الذي قهرهما وسيرهما على الوجه المخصوص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows how the two luminaries are managed and which of their possible cycles is most beneficial.
rows.anchor: بتدبيرهما والأنفع من التداوير الممكنة لهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created the stars for human use.
rows.anchor: خلقها لكم

words: لِتَهْتَدُوا۟ بِهَا فِى ظُلُمَٰتِ ٱلْبَرِّ وَٱلْبَحْرِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The darknesses may be the night on land and sea, associated with those settings, or confusing routes metaphorically called darknesses; guidance is one specified benefit after their benefits were summarized as being for people.
rows.anchor: في ظلمات الليل في البر والبحر، وإضافتها إليهما للملابسة أو في مشتبهات الطرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has explained the signs in detail, point by point.
rows.anchor: بيناها فصلا فصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who know are the ones who benefit from the detailed signs.
rows.anchor: فإنهم المنتفعون به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water was sent down from clouds or from the direction of the sky.
rows.anchor: من السحاب أو من جانب السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift to the first-person plural is a change in the mode of address.
rows.anchor: على تلوين الخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to the water.
rows.anchor: على تلوين الخطاب. { به } بالماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This means the growth of every kind of plant and displays God's power in producing diverse varieties watered by one water, as in the cited description of crops watered by one water yet differing in taste.
rows.anchor: إظهار القدرة في إنبات الأنواع المختلفة المفننة المسقية بماء واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun may refer either to the plant or to the water.
rows.anchor: من النبات أو الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khaḍir means something green, with the alternate forms akhḍar/khudr; it is the sprout emerging from the grain and branching out.
rows.anchor: شيئا أخضر يقال أخضر وخضر كأعور وعور، وهو الخارج من الحبة المتشعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The grain stacked in layers is grain growing from the green shoot, namely an ear of grain.
rows.anchor: وهو الخارج من الحبة المتشعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The syntax may mean producing palms from palms, with bunches from their spathes, or producing bunches from palm spathes; alternatively min al-nakhl predicates qinwān and min ṭalʿihā is an appositive.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون من النخل خبر قنوان ومن طلعها بدل منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qinwān are palm clusters, the plural of qinw, like ṣinwān as the plural of ṣinw.
rows.anchor: وهو الأعذاق جمع قنو كصنوان جمع صنو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qinwān is read with ḍamma on qāf, by analogy with dhiʾb/dhuʾbān, and with fatḥa as a collective noun, since fiʿlān is not a plural pattern.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بضم القاف كذئب وذؤبان وبفتحها على أنه اسم جمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clusters are near enough to reach, or densely clustered close together; mentioning these alone implies their opposite and adds a mark of favor.
rows.anchor: قريبة من المتناول، أو ملتفة قريب بعضها من بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Vineyards coordinate with 'the growth of every kind'; Nāfiʿ reads them nominative as a new subject with an implied predicate, but they cannot coordinate with palm clusters because grapes do not grow from palms.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز عطفه على { قنون } إذ العنب لا يخرج من النخل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Olives and pomegranates either coordinate with the plant growth or are accusatives of specification, because these two types were prized among the audience.
rows.anchor: أيضا عطف على نبات أو نصب على الاختصاص لعزة هذين الصنفين عندهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description may modify the pomegranate or all the fruits: some resemble one another and others differ in shape, size, color, and taste.
rows.anchor: حال من الرمان، أو من الجميع أي بعض ذلك متشابه وبعضه غير متشابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fruit to observe is the fruit of each of the plants just mentioned.
rows.anchor: أي ثمر كل واحد من ذلك

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read the tāʾ and mīm with ḍamma, treating thumur as a plural of thamarah or of thimār.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي بضم التاء والميم، وهو جمع ثمرة كخشبة وخشب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At first fruiting, the fruit is tiny and scarcely useful; at ripening it becomes large, useful, and delicious.
rows.anchor: إذا أخرج ثمره كيف يثمر ضئيلا لا يكاد ينتفع به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yanʿ means the fruit's ripeness or its ripe state; it is originally the verbal noun of ripening, or a plural of yāniʿ, and is also read with ḍamma or as yāniʿ.
rows.anchor: وإلى حال نضجه أو إلى نضيجة كيف يعود ضخما ذا نفع ولذة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The changing, diverse genera and kinds emerging from one source show a capable, wise, knowing creator who chooses among possible states and has no rival or opponent; the verse leads into rebuke of associating partners.
rows.anchor: فإن حدوث الأجناس المختلفة والأنواع المتفننة من أصل واحد ونقلها من حال إلى حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dead person is an analogy for someone God guided and rescued from error, granting the light of proofs and signs to distinguish truth from falsehood and the rightly guided from the erring.
rows.anchor: مثل به من هداه الله سبحانه وتعالى وأنقذه من الضلال وجعل له نور الحجج والآيات

rows.speaker: نافع ويعقوب
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ and Yaʿqūb read mayyitan in its original form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع ويعقوب { ميتا } على الأصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mathaluhu means his description; it is a subject whose predicate is 'in the darknesses.'
rows.anchor: كمن مثله } صفته وهو مبتدأ خبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The circumstantial clause belongs to the implied pronoun in the locative phrase, not the pronoun in mathalihi, because of the intervening material.
rows.anchor: حال من المستكن في الظرف لا من الهاء في مثله للفصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person still in darkness is the one who remains in error and never leaves it.
rows.anchor: وهو مثل لمن بقي على الضلالة لا يفارقها بحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Just as faith was made attractive to believers, the deeds of disbelievers were made attractive to them.
rows.anchor: كما زين للمؤمنين إيمانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report identifies the guided person as Ḥamza and the disbeliever as Abū Jahl.
rows.anchor: والآية نزلت في حمزة وأبي جهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report identifies the guided person as ʿUmar or ʿAmmār and the disbeliever as Abū Jahl.
rows.anchor: وقيل في عمر أو عمار وأبي جهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As in Mecca, God placed the leading criminals in every town so they would scheme there.
rows.anchor: كما جعلنا في مكة أكابر مجرميها ليمكروا فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jaʿalnā may mean 'made' with akbara mujrimiha as its two objects in reversed order, or akbar as predicate and mujrimiha as apposition; if jaʿal means enabling, mujrimiha can be genitive annexation.
rows.anchor: جعلنا } بمعنى صيرنا ومفعولاه { أكبر مجرميها } على تقديم المفعول الثاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The superlative may be singular or agree with its plural annexed noun; the recitation cited here is akbaru mujrimīhā.
rows.anchor: وأفعل التفضيل إذا أضيف جاز فيه الإفراد والمطابقة ولذلك قرىء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The leading criminals are specified because they are best able to enlist followers and use them in their schemes.
rows.anchor: وتخصيص الأكابر لأنهم أقوى على استتباع الناس والمكر بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their plotting rebounds on themselves because its harmful consequence catches them.
rows.anchor: لأن وباله يحيق بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They do not perceive that their plotting will harm them.
rows.anchor: لأن وباله يحيق بهم. { وما يشعرون } ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time expression is accusative under an omitted 'remember' or 'We say'; the pronoun denotes those gathered from both jinn and humankind.
rows.anchor: نصب باضمار اذكر أو نقول، والضمير لمن يحشر من الثقلين

rows.speaker: حفص عن عاصم وروح عن يعقوب
rows.claim: Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim and Rawḥ from Yaʿqūb read the verb with yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حفص عن عاصم وروح عن يعقوب { يحشرهم } بالياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The jinn worshipped by people here are the devils.
rows.anchor: يعني الشياطين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The jinn amassed many humans through seducing and misleading them, or gathered them as followers, as a commander amasses troops.
rows.anchor: أي من إغوائهم وإضلالهم، أو منهم جعلتموهم أتباعكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their human allies are the people who obeyed the jinn.
rows.anchor: الذين أطاعوهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans benefited from jinn by their directions to desires and how to obtain them; jinn benefited when humans obeyed them and fulfilled their aims.
rows.anchor: انتفع الإنس بالجن بأن دلوهم على الشهوات وما يتوصل به إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, humans sought the jinn's protection in deserts and dangers, while the jinn benefited from humans' admission that they could grant protection.
rows.anchor: وقيل استمتاع الإنس بهم أنهم كانوا يعوذون بهم في المفاوز وعند المخاوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The appointed term is resurrection; the speakers confess obeying Satan, following desire, and denying resurrection, and regret their state.
rows.anchor: أي البعث وهو اعتراف بما فعلوه من طاعة الشيطان واتباع الهوى وتكذيب البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mathwākum means either your dwelling or the place that contains your dwelling.
rows.anchor: منزلكم أو ذات مثواكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The circumstantial phrase 'abiding therein' is governed by mathwākum if that is a verbal noun; if it means a place, the construction is possessive.
rows.anchor: حال والعامل فيها مثواكم إن جعل مصدرا، ومعنى الإضافة إن جعل مكانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception may be the periods when they are transferred from the Fire to the intense cold, or a period before entering the Fire, when their entry is delayed.
rows.anchor: إلا الأوقات التي ينقلون فيها من النار إلى الزمهرير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is wise in His acts and knows the deeds and states of both jinn and humans.
rows.anchor: في أفعاله. { عليم } بأعمال الثقلين وأحوالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God leaves some wrongdoers to others, or makes them allies who mislead one another and accompany one another in torment as they did in the world.
rows.anchor: نكل بعضهم إلى بعض، أو نجعل بعضهم يتولى بعضا فيغويهم أولياء بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their mutual abandonment and misguidance result from their unbelief and sins.
rows.anchor: من الكفر والمعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers are humans alone; addressing humans and jinn together permits this wording, as in the verse about pearls and coral emerging from both seas though coral comes from salt water.
rows.anchor: الرسل من الإنس خاصة، لكن لما جمعوا مع الجن في الخطاب صح ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some infer from the apparent wording that messengers from each people were sent to both kinds of beings.
rows.anchor: وتعلق بظاهره قوم وقالوا بعث إلى كل من الثقلين رسل من جنسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that the jinn's messengers were human messengers sent to them, as the jinn returned to their people as warners.
rows.anchor: وقيل الرسل من الجن رسل الرسل إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers recited God's signs and warned the people about meeting the Day of Judgment.
rows.anchor: يعني يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their testimony against themselves is an admission of crime, disobedience, and unbelief, making them deserve punishment.
rows.anchor: بالجرم والعصيان وهو اعتراف منهم بالكفر واستيجاب العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse condemns their poor judgment: worldly pleasures deluded them and they wholly ignored the afterlife until forced to admit unbelief and submit to lasting torment; their fate warns the listeners.
rows.anchor: فإنهم اغتروا بالحياة الدنيوية واللذات المخدجة، وأعرضوا عن الآخرة بالكلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every possessor of a nail includes camels, wild beasts, and birds; another view includes every clawed or hoofed animal, calling the hoof a nail metaphorically.
rows.anchor: كل ماله أصبع الإبل والسباع والطيور. وقيل كل ذي مخلب وحافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The generalization of the prohibition may have been the consequence of their wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: ولعل المسبب عن الظلم تعميم التحريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forbidden fats include the omenta and kidney fats; the possessive construction strengthens the connection.
rows.anchor: الثروب وشحوم الكلى والإضافة لزيادة الربط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is fat attached to the animals' backs.
rows.anchor: إلا ما علقت بظهورهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥawāyā are the intestines, a plural of ḥāwiya, ḥāwiyāʾ, or ḥawiya.
rows.anchor: أمعاء جمع حاوية، أو حاوياء كقاصعاء وقواصع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, al-ḥawāyā coordinates with 'their fats,' with aw functioning like wāw.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو عطف على شحومهما وأو بمعنى الواو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What is mixed with bone is the fat of the tail, attached to the coccyx.
rows.anchor: هو شحم الإلية لاتصالها بالعصعص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That refers either to the prohibition or to the punishment, imposed because of their wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: التحريم أو الجزاء. { جزينهم ببغيهم } بسبب ظلمهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is truthful in what He reports, or in His promise and threat.
rows.anchor: في الإخبار أو الوعد والوعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address includes Adam, Eve, and their descendants, or Adam and Eve together with Iblīs.
rows.anchor: الخطاب لآدم وحواء وذريتهما، أو لهما ولإبليس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is repeated with Iblīs included so that their permanent companionship is understood; the speech is reported in separate parts.
rows.anchor: كرر الأمر له تبعا ليعلم أنهم قرناء أبدا وأخبر عما قال لهم متفرقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is circumstantial: they descend in a state of mutual enmity.
rows.anchor: في موضع الحال أي متعادين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mustaqarr means a place where people settle.
rows.anchor: استقرار أي موضع استقرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Matāʿ means enjoyment or provision for use.
rows.anchor: ولكم فى الأرض مستقر } استقرار أي موضع استقرار. { ومتع } وتمتع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The period lasts until each person's appointed lifespan ends.
rows.anchor: إلى أن تقضى آجالكم

words: فِيهَا تَحْيَوْنَ وَفِيهَا تَمُوتُونَ وَمِنْهَا تُخْرَجُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People live and die on earth and are brought out of it for judgment.
rows.anchor: ومنها تخرجون } للجزاء وقرأ حمزة والكسائي

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وابن ذكوان
rows.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Ibn Dhakwān read the phrase with fatḥa on tāʾ and ḍamma on rāʾ, an active form; the same reading occurs in 43:11.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وابن ذكوان { ومنها تخرجون } ، وفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time clause is coordinated with the earlier mention of when the Sabbath-breakers transgressed.
rows.anchor: وإذ قالت } عطف على { إذ يعدون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The group are the town's righteous people, who persisted in admonishing until they despaired of the others taking heed.
rows.anchor: جماعة من أهل القرية يعني صلحاءهم الذين اجتهدوا في موعظتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The questioners may be overstating that admonition cannot help, asking why the admonishers continue, or speaking as a reformed group to those who have not reformed; another view makes them members of the doomed faction responding mockingly.
rows.anchor: قالوه مبالغة في أن الوعظ لا ينفع فيهم، أو سؤالا عن علة الوعظ ونفعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhl ikuhum here means that God will destroy or annihilate them.
rows.anchor: لم تعظون قوما الله مهلكهم } مخترمهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The severe punishment is in the afterlife because of their persistent disobedience.
rows.anchor: في الآخرة لتماديهم في العصيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The advisers answer that they warn people to establish their excuse before God and avoid being accused of neglecting the duty to forbid wrong.
rows.anchor: موعظتنا إنهاء عذر إلى الله حتى لا ننسب إلى تفريط في النهي عن المنكر

rows.speaker: حفص
rows.claim: Ḥafṣ reads maʿdhiratan in the accusative, as a verbal noun or causal expression: they offered an excuse or admonished as their excuse.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حفص { معذرة } بالنصب على المصدر أو العلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They hope the sinners will desist; despair of their reform only comes with their destruction.
rows.anchor: إذ اليأس لا يحصل إلا بالهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They 'forgot' by abandoning the admonition as if they had forgotten it.
rows.anchor: تركوا ترك الناسي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is what their righteous advisers had warned them about.
rows.anchor: ما ذكرهم به صلحاؤهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God rescued those who forbade evil and seized the wrongdoers for transgression and disobeying God's command.
rows.anchor: بالاعتداء ومخالفة أمر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baʾīs means severe, from the root denoting severity.
rows.anchor: شديد فعيل من بؤس يبؤس بؤسا إذا اشتد

rows.speaker: أبو بكر، ابن عامر، نافع
rows.claim: Abū Bakr reads biʾyis on the pattern fiʿayl; Ibn ʿĀmir reads biʾs with a still hamza, also reported as a softened adjective; Nāfiʿ reads bīs by turning hamza to yāʾ or by converting a verb of blame into a name.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو بكر " بيئس " على فيعل كضيغم، وابن عامر «بئس» بكسر الباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other readings assimilate a hamza changed to yāʾ, lighten the form like hayyin, or use bāʾis on the pattern fāʿil.
rows.anchor: وقرىء " بيس " كريس على قلب الهمزة ثم ادغامها و " بيس " بالتخفيف كهين وبائس كفاعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their punishment came because of their disobedience.
rows.anchor: بسبب فسقهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They arrogantly refused to give up what they had been forbidden, as in the parallel description in 7:77.
rows.anchor: تكبروا عن ترك ما نهوا عنه كقوله تعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's command to become apes is effective by His word alone, as in the statement that when He wills a thing, He says 'Be,' and it is.
rows.anchor: تكبروا عن ترك ما نهوا عنه كقوله تعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surface sequence suggests severe punishment first and transformation after their later defiance; alternatively, the second verse explains and specifies the first.
rows.anchor: والظاهر يقتضي أن الله تعالى عذبهم أولا بعذاب شديد فعتوا بعد ذلك فمسخهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the admonishers, despairing of reform, separated from the offenders with a wall and gate; when no offenders came out, they entered and found them transformed into apes. The apes did not recognize kin, but recognized the humans, circled them weeping and sniffing their clothes, and died after three days.
rows.anchor: فقسموا القرية بجدار فيه باب مطروق، فأصبحوا يوما ولم يخرج إليهم أحد

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says their hearts, not their bodies, were transformed into apes.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد مسخت قلوبهم لا أبدانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ṭāʾif is a satanic touch or whisper, from ṭāfa as if circling without affecting the pious, or from the expression for a passing vision or thought.
rows.anchor: لمة منه، وهو اسم فاعل من طاف يطوف كأنها طافت بهم ودارت حولهم

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو والكسائي ويعقوب
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, al-Kisāʾī, and Yaʿqūb read ṭayf, as a verbal noun or a shortened pronunciation like layn/hayn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو والكسائي ويعقوب «طيف» على أنه مصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan is generic here, which is why the pronoun referring to him is plural.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالشيطان الجنس ولذلك جمع ضميره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They remember what God commanded and what He prohibited.
rows.anchor: ما أمر الله به ونهى عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering lets them see their errors and Satan's schemes, so they guard against them and do not follow Satan in them.
rows.anchor: بسبب التذكر مواقع الخطأ ومكايد الشيطان فيتحرزون عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse reinforces and confirms the preceding discussion.
rows.anchor: والآية تأكيد وتقرير لما قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse was revealed when people spoke during prayer; they were ordered to listen to the imam's recitation and remain silent.
rows.anchor: نزلت في الصلاة كانوا يتكلمون فيها فأمروا باستماع قراءة الإمام والإنصات له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent wording requires listening and silence whenever the Qur'an is recited, without restriction to prayer.
rows.anchor: وظاهر اللفظ يقتضي وجوبهما حيث يقرأ القرآن مطلقا

rows.speaker: عامة العلماء
rows.claim: The majority of scholars consider listening and silence recommended outside prayer.
rows.anchor: وعامة العلماء على استحبابهما خارج الصلاة

rows.speaker: من لا يرى وجوب القراءة على المأموم
rows.claim: Those who infer that the follower in prayer is not obliged to recite rely on this verse, but al-Bayḍāwī calls the argument weak.
rows.anchor: واحتج به من لا يرى وجوب القراءة على المأموم وهو ضعيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Responding to God and the Messenger means obeying them.
rows.anchor: استجيبوا لله وللرسول } بالطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun is singular because the context just mentioned one caller, and God's call is heard through the Messenger.
rows.anchor: وحد الضمير فيه لما سبق ولأن دعوة الله تسمع من الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet passed Abū while he was praying, called him, and Abū hurried in his prayer to answer; when asked why, he said he had been praying, and the Prophet cited what had been revealed to him.
rows.anchor: روي أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام مر على أبي وهو يصلي فدعاه فعجل في صلاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that answering the Prophet does not interrupt prayer, since prayer itself is a response to God and the Messenger.
rows.anchor: فقيل هذا لأن إجابته لا تقطع الصلاة فإن الصلاة أيضا إجابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that the call concerned an urgent matter; a worshipper may interrupt prayer for such a matter. The apparent hadith favors the first explanation.
rows.anchor: وقيل لأن دعاءه كان لأمر لا يحتمل التأخير وللمصلي أن يقطع الصلاة لمثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What gives life may be religious knowledge, which revives the heart while ignorance is its death; a cited poem calls the ignorant person dead and his clothing a shroud.
rows.anchor: من العلوم الدينية فإنها حياة القلب والجهل موته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase can also mean beliefs and deeds that grant eternal life in lasting bliss, jihad that preserves the community from defeat and death, or martyrdom, as in 3:169.
rows.anchor: أو مما يورثكم الحياة الأبدية في النعيم الدائم من العقائد والأعمال، أو من الجهاد

words: أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَحُولُ بَيْنَ ٱلْمَرْءِ وَقَلْبِهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording pictures God's extreme nearness to a person, as in 50:16.
rows.anchor: تمثيل لغاية قربه من العبد

words: أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَحُولُ بَيْنَ ٱلْمَرْءِ وَقَلْبِهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It warns that God knows the heart's hidden contents, some of which its owner may overlook.
rows.anchor: وتنبيه على أنه مطلع على مكنونات القلوب مما عسى يغفل عنه صاحبها

words: أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَحُولُ بَيْنَ ٱلْمَرْءِ وَقَلْبِهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may urge prompt sincerity and purification before God separates a person from the heart through death or another cause.
rows.anchor: أو حث على المبادرة إلى إخلاص القلوب وتصفيتها قبل أن يحول الله بينه وبين قلبه بالموت

words: أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَحُولُ بَيْنَ ٱلْمَرْءِ وَقَلْبِهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may portray God's control over the heart: He can undo intentions and change aims, preventing unbelief for one destined for felicity or faith for one destined for misery.
rows.anchor: أو تصوير وتخييل لتملكه على العبد قلبه فيفسخ عزائمه ويغير مقاصده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading doubles the rāʾ after deleting the hamza and transferring its vowel to rāʾ, applying connected speech like a pause in a dialect that uses this doubling.
rows.anchor: وقرىء " بين المرء " بالتشديد على حذف الهمزة وإلقاء حركتها على الراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All will be gathered to God, who will recompense them for their deeds.
rows.anchor: فيجازيكم بأعمالكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time clause is an appositive to 'the day of the Criterion' in 8:41.
rows.anchor: الدنيا } بدل من { يوم الفرقان } ، والعدوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word for riverbank has three case-vowel forms; the common forms are ḍamma and kasra, with the latter read by Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, and Yaʿqūb.
rows.anchor: والعدوة بالحركات الثلاث شط الوادي وقد قرىء بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-quṣwā is the farther bank from Medina, the feminine of al-aqṣā; the expected form would change wāw to yāʾ, but the original form remains, like al-qawd, and is more common than al-quṣyā.
rows.anchor: البعدى من المدينة، تأنيث الأقصى وكان قياسه قلب الواو ياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The caravan means either the trade caravan itself or its leaders.
rows.anchor: أي العير أو قوادها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This means in a lower place, namely the shore; it is an adverb functioning as predicate, and the clause is circumstantial to the preceding locative.
rows.anchor: في مكان أسفل من مكانكم يعني الساحل، وهو منصوب على الظرف واقع موقع الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning the caravan displays the enemy's strength, support from the caravan, resolve to fight for it and hold their positions, against the Muslims' weakness and disorganization; the near bank was soft, difficult to cross, and had no water, unlike the far bank.
rows.anchor: وفائدتها الدلالة على قوة العدو واستظهارهم بالركب وحرصهم على المقاتلة عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If both sides had arranged a battle after seeing the imbalance, the Muslims would have failed to keep the appointment from fear and despair; the outcome therefore revealed a miraculous divine victory and increased their faith and gratitude.
rows.anchor: لو تواعدتم أنتم وهم القتال ثم علمتم حالكم وحالهم لاختلفتم أنتم في الميعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God brought them together without an appointment to fulfill His decree: aiding His allies and defeating His enemies.
rows.anchor: حقيقا بأن يفعل وهو نصر أوليائه وقهر أعدائه

words: لِّيَهْلِكَ مَنْ هَلَكَ عَنۢ بَيِّنَةٍۢ وَيَحْيَىٰ مَنْ حَىَّ عَنۢ بَيِّنَةٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may mean that some die and others live after witnessing clear proof, leaving no excuse, since Badr was a manifest sign; or that unbelief and faith emerge from clear proof, using death and life metaphorically for those states.
rows.anchor: ليموت من يموت عن بينة عاينها ويعيش من يعيش عن حجة شاهدها

words: لِّيَهْلِكَ مَنْ هَلَكَ وَيَحْيَىٰ مَنْ حَىَّ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who perish or live may be approaching that fate, or may be people so described in God's knowledge and decree.
rows.anchor: والمراد بمن هلك ومن حي المشارف للهلاك والحياة، أو من هذا حاله في علم الله وقضائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is also read with fatḥa on yāʾ; Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ, Abū Bakr, and Yaʿqūb read ḥayya with the two yāʾs pronounced separately.
rows.anchor: وقرىء " ليهلك " بالفتح وقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو بكر ويعقوب من " حيي " بفك الإدغام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears the unbeliever's confession and knows his punishment, and hears the believer and knows his reward; the paired attributes suit speech and belief.
rows.anchor: بكفر من كفر وعقابه، وإيمان من آمن وثوابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These are some of those who stayed behind, who admitted their sins instead of making false excuses.
rows.anchor: ولم يعتذروا عن تخلفهم بالمعاذير الكاذبة، وهم طائفة من المتخلفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says they tied themselves to pillars in the mosque after learning what had been revealed about those who stayed behind. The Prophet saw them after his customary prayer, heard they would not release themselves until he did, swore he would wait for a command about them, then the verse came and he released them.
rows.anchor: أوثقوا أنفسهم على سواري المسجد لما بلغهم ما نزل في المتخلفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their good deed was showing regret and confessing sin; their bad deed was staying behind and siding with hypocrites.
rows.anchor: الفعل الصالح الذي هو إظهار الندم والاعتراف بالذنب بآخر سيء هو التخلف وموافقة أهل النفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conjunction wāw may mean biʾ, as in the idiom of selling a sheep for a sheep and a dirham, or show that each act is mixed with the other.
rows.anchor: والواو إما بمعنى الباء كما في قولهم بعت الشاء شاة ودرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may accept their repentance, which is indicated by their confession of their sins.
rows.anchor: أن يقبل توبتهم وهي مدلول عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God overlooks the penitent's sins and graciously favors the penitent.
rows.anchor: يتجاوز عن التائب ويتفضل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to the Day of Judgment.
rows.anchor: أي اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The delay lasts until a finite appointed period ends; an annexed noun is omitted, and 'the term' refers to the whole period of postponement rather than its endpoint alone.
rows.anchor: إلا لانتهاء مدة معدودة متناهية على حذف المضاف وإرادة مدة التأجيل كلها بالأجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The coming may be that of requital or the Day itself (with yawm meaning 'when'), or God, as in the cited passages.
rows.anchor: على أن { يوم } بمعنى حين أو الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir, ʿĀṣim, and Ḥamza read the verb without its final yāʾ, relying on the kasra in its place.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة { يأت } بحذف الياء اجتزاء عنها بالكسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No soul speaks what can benefit and save it, whether an answer or an intercession.
rows.anchor: لا تتكلم بما ينفع وينجي من جواب أو شفاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause 'no soul speaks' governs the time adverb; alternatively, the adverb depends on an implied 'remember' or on an omitted verb meaning 'at the end.'
rows.anchor: وهو الناصب للظرف ويحتمل نصبه بإضمار اذكر أو بالانتهاء المحذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The permission is God's, as in 78:38; this may be a different standing from 77:35–36, or only truthful answers are permitted while false excuses are barred.
rows.anchor: أو المأذون فيه هي الجوابات الحقة والممنوع عنه هي الأعذار الباطلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wretched are destined for Hell under the threat and the happy for Paradise under the promise; 'them' means those at the gathering, inferred from 'no soul speaks' or meaning people.
rows.anchor: وجبت له النار بمقتضى الوعيد. { وسعيد } وجبت له الجنة بموجب الوعد
